learning_outcomes.text: Have systematic knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and aspects for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve machine calculation, design and testing problems using established methods.
Be able to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out mechanical designs that meet specific requirements.
Have an understanding of the different methods for the calculation, design and testing of machines and the ability to use them.
Have technical and laboratory skills in the design and testing of machines.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve problems of machine calculation, design and testing.
Have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques in the calculation, design and testing of machines and their limitations.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering field.
Adequate knowledge of their engineering field, including some knowledge at the forefront of their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to meet required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.

syllabus_topics: Resistance to motion on straight and horizontal tracks. Davis equation.
Power at wheel rim, resistance power, and drawbar power.
Calculation of stresses in the track. Zimmerman's Theory I.
assessment_rules: The continuous assessment consists of a written test covering half of the course, weighted at 50%. The final assessment consists of a written test covering the part of the course not evaluated in continuous assessment, weighted at 50%. Lab practicals are mandatory; failure to complete them results in failing the course in the ordinary call. In the extraordinary call, students may take a practical exam. Failing this practical exam, even if the theory exam is passed, results in failing the course.
